To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lithium-sensitive GSK3β is a powerful regulator, which increases the function of excitatory amino-acids transporters EAATs 3 and 4.
GSK3ß increases EAAT3 and 4 mediated glutamate uptake, and that lithium decreases GSK3ß mediated increase of glutamate uptake.
GSK3ß upregulates EAAT3 and 4 and that lithium-sensitive GSK3 activity down-regulates EAAT3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the lithium effect on excitability.
the role of GSK3β on EAATs.
the role of GSK3 in the regulation of glutamate transport by the excitatory glutamate transporters EAAT1 and EAAT4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lithium-sensitive GSK3β is a powerful regulator for excitatory amino acid carriers EAAT3 and 4.
lithium-sensitive GSK3β is a potent regulator of excitatory neurotransmitter transporters, and that lithium-sensitive regulation of EAATs may contribute to the therapeutic action of lithium.
the present data suggest that GSK3ß activity is required for the full activity of EAAT3 or 4, and that lithium may decrease the activity of the EAAT3 and 4 isoforms, by inhibiting GSK3ß.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lithium-sensitive GSK3b up-regulates the excitatory amino acid carriers EAAT3 and 4.
lithium sensitive GSK3ß increases EAAT3 and 4 activity, which may contribute to the anticonvulsant effect of lithium.
lithium sensitive GSK3ß up-regulates EAAT3 and thus decreases glutamate excitotoxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lithium sensitive glycogen synthase-3ß is a regulator of excitatory glutamate uptake by the excitatory neurotransmitter transporters EAAT-3 and EAAT-4.
GSK3ß increases the activity of EAAT3 or/and EAAT4.
GSK3ß increases IEAAT by increasing the maximal IEAATT without significantly affecting affinity.
